title: Simple Regret for Nested Prediction Sets with Response-Selected Counterfactual Labels

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed an informal matched full-versus-blind policy-regret frontier and response-selection correction; the governing D0.5 halt assessed subfield (6.8) below the field floor (7.4), with no bounded improvement directive. Decision review passed and all seven cited leaves verified, but math review remains revise: the M=2 converse omits a changed observed cell, so its KL constant 16, theorem constant 1/512 and complete headline proof are uncertified. Independent main validity review finds a plausible local baseline-KL/Pinsker/testing repair preserves the rate but cannot earn field; no Lean formalization or delivery certification was performed.
tldr: Correct counterfactual labels can be response-selected calibration observations. In a prespecified uniform logging experiment with interval-valued individual success paths, the causal target is the population accuracy of one fixed nested-set action. The proposed full-record minimax simple-regret frontier is \(r_{\mathrm{full}}(n,K)\), with a truth-entry quantile screen and original-record success scores as the attaining construction; deleting truth-entry marks gives the separate blind frontier target \(r_{\mathrm{blind}}(n,K)\). A common-truth legal packing is the full-record converse construction. The selection characterization is proved, including exact centering, tie-sensitive ranking conditions, raw-ratio convergence and an unbiased observable correction. The norm-selected original-likelihood policy has a separate coarse-risk bracket; whether it attains the screened-score frontier uniformly over atoms and sparse strata remains unresolved. The consumer is offline deployment-size calibration for prediction-set decision support.
gap: Wu and Li give smooth contextual prediction-set simple-regret bounds under adaptive allocation. Straitouri and Gomez Rodriguez give an adaptive cumulative-regret bound. Auction screening and marked-current-status theory supply relevant tools. The remaining target is the explicit all-\((n,K)\) full-versus-blind decision-information frontier for immutable uniform logging over the entire arbitrary interval-law simplex; this is a different experiment, with no smoothness or local-ordering restriction.
fill: An explicit screened original-score learner is paired with lawful full-experiment testing alternatives. The proposal also distinguishes population centering from same-person label validity and poses the natural original-likelihood policy's uniform risk as a separate open question.
